known_hazards_for_machine_consumers: DO NOT machine-check the reconciliation identity off len(refusals). The per-sport 'refusals' arrays are not row counts: MLB has 11 entries against n_refused=0 (all field-level, inside otherwise-canonical rows) and NFL has 12 against n_refused=10 (10 row-level + 1 slate-level + 1 starter-level). n_canonical IS NOT A UNIFORM QUALITY SIGNAL ACROSS SPORTS. Three different bars were applied: WNBA's 4 canonical rows rest on a retained git artifact; MLB's 15 rest on search identification only, while its own refusal states the slate 'must not be used to bind results'; NFL and CFB scored 0 canonical on that same class of evidence. Compare within a sport, never across.

normalization_applied.residual_hazard: MLB legitimately mixes MLB_GAMEPK (5 rows) and ESPN_GAMEID (10 rows) in one column. The namespace is load-bearing, not cosmetic — downstream must branch on it.
normalization_applied.rule: all ids normalized to '<ID_SPACE>:<integer>' with ID_SPACE in ['MLB_GAMEPK', 'ESPN_GAMEID']; a bare integer is a hard error at write time
normalization_applied.why: The four per-sport reports emitted the same ESPN id space in four encodings — 'ESPN_GAMEID:401816711' (MLB), bare '401857180' (WNBA), 'espn:401873302' (NFL), 'ESPN:401868261' (CFB). The bare WNBA integer is the highest-risk form: it is indistinguishable from an MLB gamePk column value.
